concept.name: Quorum Read/Write Tuning

relationships.description: Connects Quorum Read/Write Tuning to caching in the broader engineering catalog.

spark.summary: Quorum tuning balances strong consistency, tail latency, and fault tolerance in replicated databases by choosing replication factor N, write quorum W, and read quorum R—where W + R > N guarantees read-your-writes overlap.
spark.keyTakeaway: Tune W + R > N (typically N=3, W=2, R=2) for strong overlap, or drop to W=1 / R=1 only when you explicitly accept stale reads and asynchronous read-repair.

concept.whyItMatters: Every distributed datastore without a single strict leader (Dynamo, Cassandra, ScyllaDB, Riak) forces an explicit per-query trade-off between consistency, availability, and p99 latency. Misconfigured quorums either cause silent lost updates and stale reads when W + R <= N, or trigger avoidable outages during rolling restarts when W or R is set too high.
whenToUse: Tuning Dynamo-style leaderless databases (Cassandra, ScyllaDB, DynamoDB-like architectures) per workload using N, W, and R.
Balancing p99 read/write latency against durability in multi-AZ or multi-region clusters (LOCAL_QUORUM vs EACH_QUORUM).
Designing degraded-mode fallback policies when a datacenter loses one or more replica nodes.
whenNotToUse: Consensus-backed strongly linearizable databases (etcd, CockroachDB, Spanner) where Raft/Paxos mandates majority (floor(N/2)+1) and cannot be weakened per-query.
Single-node databases or strict primary-standby setups without multi-replica quorum routing.
Transactional multi-key ACID workflows where leaderless LWW (Last-Write-Wins) quorums still allow write skew without lightweight transactions.
keyPoints: Strict overlap requires W + R > N so at least one replica in the read quorum holds the latest acknowledged write.
Preventing concurrent write conflicts requires W > N / 2; otherwise two disjoint write quorums can succeed simultaneously.
For N=3, QUORUM (W=2, R=2) tolerates 1 node failure for both reads and writes while capping tail latency at the 2nd-fastest replica.
W + R > N does not guarantee linearizability in Dynamo/Cassandra without monotonic clocks or Paxos/LWT, because partial writes can still leak to subsequent reads.
Background repair (read repair, hinted handoff, Merkle-tree anti-entropy) is mandatory to heal lagging replicas even under strict quorums.

examples.title: Cassandra Session Store: N=3, LOCAL_QUORUM (W=2, R=2)
examples.scenario: A user-profile service stores sessions in a 3-AZ Cassandra cluster (N=3) and needs to survive a single-AZ maintenance restart without stale reads.
examples.outcome: With W=2 and R=2 (2+2 > 3), 1 down node causes zero errors, p99 latency tracks the 2nd-fastest AZ (~4 ms), and read-your-writes holds.

examples.title: Flash-Sale Degradation Trap: Dropping to W=1, R=1
examples.scenario: To shave 3 ms off checkout latency, a team switches an inventory counter from QUORUM to ONE (W=1, R=1) with N=3.
examples.outcome: Because 1 + 1 <= 3, readers hit stale replicas before async replication arrives, overselling limited stock and losing updates under LWW clock skew.

tradeOffs.pro: Higher W and R (e.g., W=2, R=2 for N=3) enforce overlapping quorums and immediate read-repair on digest mismatch.
tradeOffs.con: Wait time is bounded by the W-th or R-th slowest replica instead of the fastest replica (W=1/R=1).

tradeOffs.pro: Increasing N from 3 to 5 with W=3, R=3 survives 2 simultaneous node failures (1 planned + 1 crash).
tradeOffs.con: Increases storage footprint by 67% and cross-node write amplification.

tradeOffs.pro: EACH_QUORUM guarantees every datacenter sees writes before acknowledgment.
tradeOffs.con: Adds full cross-region RTT (~70-150 ms) to every write and fails writes if any remote DC loses quorum.

failureModes.name: Sloppy Quorum Stale Read
failureModes.description: When hinted handoff accepts writes on non-home nodes during a partition, a strict R quorum on home nodes misses the hinted write.
failureModes.mitigation: Disable sloppy quorums for strongly consistent workloads and rely on strict home-replica quorums.

failureModes.name: NTP Clock Skew Under Last-Write-Wins (LWW)
failureModes.description: A node with a clock skewed +500 ms ahead wins every LWW tie-break, silently dropping newer writes from other coordinators.
failureModes.mitigation: Enforce tight NTP/chrony sync, use Hybrid Logical Clocks (HLC), or use Paxos/LWT for contended keys.

failureModes.name: Partial Write Leakage (Non-Linearizable Read)
failureModes.description: A write fails after updating 1 of 2 required replicas (returning an error to the client), yet a subsequent R=2 read sees and repairs that partial write.
failureModes.mitigation: Document that W+R>N gives eventual/read-your-writes only for acknowledged writes; use LWT/Raft if atomic rollback is required.

failureModes.name: Hinted Handoff Storm on Recovery
failureModes.description: A node down for >3 hours exceeds max_hint_window_in_ms, or floods the cluster with gigabytes of replayed hints upon rejoin.
failureModes.mitigation: Run scheduled incremental Merkle-tree repairs (nodetool repair) within gc_grace_seconds and throttle hint replay.

commonMistakes: Assuming W + R > N alone provides strict serializability/linearizability in leaderless LWW stores.
Using N=3, W=3, R=1 for write-heavy durability without realizing a single dead node halts 100% of writes.
Using ALL in multi-AZ clusters, turning any single-node GC pause into a cluster-wide p99 spike or outage.
Skipping periodic anti-entropy repairs, leading to 'zombie deletes' when tombstones expire past gc_grace_seconds.
Choosing EACH_QUORUM for writes when LOCAL_QUORUM + async cross-DC replication meets business RPO.

sections.content:
## The idea

In a leaderless replicated store (popularized by Amazon's Dynamo paper and implemented in Apache Cassandra and ScyllaDB), every key is replicated across `N` nodes. Rather than locking all `N` replicas, a coordinator fans out reads and writes in parallel and returns as soon as `W` (write quorum) or `R` (read quorum) replicas acknowledge.

By the pigeonhole principle, if **`W + R > N`**, any read quorum of size `R` must intersect any write quorum of size `W` in at least one node. That overlapping node carries the highest timestamped value, allowing the coordinator to return fresh data and trigger **read repair** on stale replicas.

## Concrete walkthrough

Trace a write followed by a read on a **Cassandra `N=3, W=2, R=2` (`QUORUM`)** cluster:

1. **Write (`W=2`)**: Client sends `UPDATE balance = 500 (ts=102)` to the coordinator. The coordinator forwards the mutation to replicas `R1`, `R2`, and `R3`.
2. **Quorum satisfied**: `R1` (`2 ms`) and `R2` (`4 ms`) persist to commitlog + memtable and ack. `R3` is experiencing a `40 ms` GC pause. The coordinator returns `200 OK` to the client at `4 ms`.
3. **Read (`R=2`)**: Another client reads `balance` with `R=2`. The coordinator requests the full row from `R1` and a cryptographic digest from `R3` (optimizing bandwidth).
4. **Digest mismatch & read repair**: `R1` has `ts=102 (500)` while `R3` has `ts=101 (400)`. The digests mismatch. The coordinator fetches full data from both, returns `500` (`ts=102`) to the client, and issues an async read-repair write (`ts=102`) to heal `R3`.

sections.eyebrow: 03 / Why W + R > N is not full linearizability
sections.content:
## Why W + R > N is not full linearizability

A common misconception is that `W + R > N` makes a Dynamo/Cassandra cluster linearizable. Two subtleties break linearizability:

1. **Failed-write leakage**: If a write updates `R1` and then times out before reaching `R2`, the client receives a `WriteTimeoutException`. However, `R1` still holds the new value; a later `R=2` read hitting `R1` and `R3` will return—and repair—the "failed" write.
2. **Concurrent write races**: Without Paxos/Raft (`SERIAL` / `LOCAL_SERIAL`), two concurrent writers rely on physical wall-clock LWW timestamps, which can invert ordering under NTP drift.

## Common quorum profiles (N=3 and N=5)

| Profile | N / W / R | Tolerated Failures (W / R) | Tail Latency | Best Workload Fit |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Balanced Quorum** | `3 / 2 / 2` | 1 / 1 | 2nd-fastest of 3 | General OLTP, user profiles, sessions |
| **Read-Optimized** | `3 / 3 / 1` | 0 / 2 | Fastest of 3 (reads) | Read-heavy catalogs where write downtime is rare |
| **Write-Optimized** | `3 / 1 / 3` | 2 / 0 | Fastest of 3 (writes) | High-ingest telemetry that tolerates slow/brittle reads |
| **Eventual Fast** | `3 / 1 / 1` | 2 / 2 | Fastest of 3 | Append-only logs, metrics, non-critical caches |
| **High-Resilience** | `5 / 3 / 3` | 2 / 2 | 3rd-fastest of 5 | Survives 1 planned maintenance + 1 sudden crash |

## Failure modes

Quorum systems degrade in four predictable ways:

- **Rolling-restart outage on `W=N`**: Setting `W=3` for `N=3` means any single-node upgrade or reboot blocks all writes.
- **Cross-region latency explosion**: Using `EACH_QUORUM` forces writes to wait for remote-DC RTTs (~80–150 ms) and fails writes if any DC loses a majority.
- **Clock-skew overwrite**: A coordinator with a fast clock stamps writes 1 second in the future, making every subsequent write from normal nodes silently lose LWW.
- **Zombie deletes**: If a down node misses a tombstone and rejoins after `gc_grace_seconds` (default 10 days) without repair, old data resurrects.

## Multi-datacenter quorum tuning

In multi-region deployments (`RF=3` per DC), prefer **`LOCAL_QUORUM` for both reads and writes** paired with sticky regional routing. Clients get ~3–5 ms local latency and strong intra-DC consistency, while cross-DC replication proceeds asynchronously. Reserve `EACH_QUORUM` or `SERIAL` (Paxos LWT) strictly for global uniqueness checks or financial balances.

## Practical checklist

- [ ] Verify `W + R > N` and `W > N/2` for any table requiring read-your-writes consistency.
- [ ] Use `LOCAL_QUORUM` instead of `QUORUM` or `ALL` in multi-DC clusters to avoid cross-region tail latency.
- [ ] Schedule incremental Merkle-tree anti-entropy repairs (`nodetool repair`) well within `gc_grace_seconds`.
- [ ] Monitor NTP/chrony clock drift across all coordinators and use Paxos/LWT (`SERIAL`) for contended updates.
- [ ] Upgrade to `N=5, W=3, R=3` for tier-0 tables that must survive a rolling restart plus an unexpected node failure.

interviewProblems.title: Quorum Read/Write Tuning
interviewProblems.scenarioPrompt: Design a production system that depends on Quorum Read/Write Tuning. What invariants, failure modes, and observability do you require?
interviewProblems.sampleDefense: Start from invariants, choose the pattern that preserves them, and add metrics for the known failure modes.
commonPitfalls: Optimizing throughput before defining correctness boundaries.

steps.title: 1. Normal Request Ingress
steps.explanation: Quorum tuning balances strong consistency, tail latency, and fault tolerance in replicated databases by choosing replication factor N, write quorum W, and read quorum R—where W + R > N guarantees read-your-writes overlap.

steps.title: 2. Core Execution & State Lookup
steps.explanation: Replica 2 (AZ-b) applies the primary invariant and coordinates with Replica 3 (AZ-c).

steps.title: 3. Scale Spike / Failure Injection
steps.explanation: Under a 10x burst, Replica 3 (AZ-c) experiences contention and tail-latency amplification.

steps.title: 4. Mitigation & Steady Recovery
steps.explanation: Disable sloppy quorums for strongly consistent workloads and rely on strict home-replica quorums.

tipsAndTricks: Core mental model: Tune W + R > N (typically N=3, W=2, R=2) for strong overlap, or drop to W=1 / R=1 only when you explicitly accept stale reads and asynchronous read-repair.
Avoid trap: Assuming W + R > N alone provides strict serializability/linearizability in leaderless LWW stores.
Avoid trap: Using N=3, W=3, R=1 for write-heavy durability without realizing a single dead node halts 100% of writes.
When to reach for it: Tuning Dynamo-style leaderless databases (Cassandra, ScyllaDB, DynamoDB-like architectures) per workload using N, W, and R.
When to reach for it: Balancing p99 read/write latency against durability in multi-AZ or multi-region clusters (LOCAL_QUORUM vs EACH_QUORUM).

putItTogether.title: Putting Quorum Tuning Together
putItTogether.summary: Tune W + R > N (typically N=3, W=2, R=2) for strong overlap, or drop to W=1 / R=1 only when you explicitly accept stale reads and asynchronous read-repair.
steps: Establish baseline invariants for Quorum Tuning before scaling.
Isolate hot paths with caching, backpressure, or partitioning.
Verify failure modes with synthetic load & chaos checks.
putItTogether.outcome: With W=2 and R=2 (2+2 > 3), 1 down node causes zero errors, p99 latency tracks the 2nd-fastest AZ (~4 ms), and read-your-writes holds.
